headline: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomics nominate prognostic cancer biomarkers
label: Integrative Multiomics Cancer Biomarkers
summary: Public multi-omics resources now allow single-cell and spatial layers to be added to bulk prognostic models across tumor types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational integration of public resources such as TCGA, GEO, and SEER with single-cell, scATAC-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to nominate prognostic genes, immune-associated signatures, and cell states across tumor types. SIGLNCOS identifies 667 cellular-signature lncRNAs across 31 cancers, and CDState infers malignant cell states from bulk RNA-seq across 33 TCGA types. Other items resolve specific niches and mediators, including a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche linked to neoadjuvant chemotherapy non-response in bladder cancer and SERPINE1 as an endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in HNSCC. Experimental follow-up is limited; TROAP depletion in osteosarcoma is one example, while most items remain computational. What is new relative to bulk-only prognostic models is the layering of single-cell and spatial context onto survival-linked gene sets.
